text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Norway's state-owned telecommunication company Telenor will most probably win a contract to develop a new mobile-phone network in Germany. The contract is worth between one and two billion crowns.
-Despite increased consumption in general, Norwegians spent less money on TV, radios and other electrical equipment in 1996 than 1995.
-Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg says it is important to watch signs of a possible overheating of the strong Norwegian economy.

-Few believe that the central bank will manage to bring back the appreciating crown to its previous, weaker levels. The question is what central bank governor Kjell Storvik will say in his annual speech tonight.
-Oslo Bishop Andreas Aarflot has appointed a committee to look into the possibility of separating the protestant church from the state.

-Norway's central bank Governor Kjell Storvik and his Islandic colleague Birger Gunnarsson are the only western central bank chiefs outside the ERM who still aim at securing a stable exchange rate for their currencies.
-Norway's northern fishing industry lost 200 million crowns because of stormy weather in January.
